name: Fushimi Inari to the summit of Inariyama (稲荷山)
why: Up the holy mountain of the rice god through tunnels of vermilion torii, past fox statues and moss-covered shrine mounds, to the 233 m top of the Higashiyama hills.
book: Free and always open. JR Inari station (5 minutes from Kyoto) is in front of the main gate. The lower gates are packed from 09:00: start early, or come late afternoon.
water: Tea houses and vending machines along the path up to Yotsutsuji and beyond; toilets at the main shrine and on the way.
dangers: Thousands of steps, slippery in rain.
Summer heat and humidity under the gates: carry water and go early.
Above Yotsutsuji the lights are few: bring a torch if you walk at dusk.
turnaround: Short on time or legs: turn back at Yotsutsuji, the view over Kyoto is there; the summit loop adds about an hour.

points.name: Senbon torii
points.note: Behind the main hall, two parallel rows of closely packed gates start the climb; each gate was given by a person or a company, with their name on the back.

points.name: Yotsutsuji crossing
points.note: The four-way junction about halfway up, 30-45 minutes from the start, with a tea house and the view over south Kyoto. The summit loop starts here.

points.name: Inari summit
points.note: Ichinomine, 233 m: the highest shrine, in the trees, no view. Reached by the east side of the loop; go down by the other side past the other peaks to Yotsutsuji, then the way you came.
